title: Evidence-gated evaluation of cross-dataset battery state-of-health transfer with a diagnostic state-of-charge proxy
abstract: Lower prediction error on an unseen battery dataset does not necessarily demonstrate transferable degradation learning. A model may better align its prediction level without improving its ability to follow changes in individual cells. This study presents an evidence-gated framework for evaluating cross-dataset battery state-of-health (SOH) transfer. It distinguishes absolute-error reduction from centered-error improvement and within-cell rank association, with uncertainty assessed at the cell level. Each dataset is held out in turn, and access to target information follows explicit rules. Few-shot adaptation uses early-cycle observations and a fixed future evaluation horizon. Calibration baselines help interpret apparent gains, while a trace-derived state-of-charge proxy serves only offline diagnostic purposes. Results across four public datasets do not establish consistent transfer behavior. Selected settings combine lower error with positive within-cell associations, but their small magnitudes provide only limited tracking evidence. Other settings yield inconclusive or inverse associations. A target with narrow, high-SOH-dominated support permits diagnostic interpretation only. Greater model capacity or auxiliary supervision does not uniformly resolve this heterogeneity. Changing the reference-capacity definition also alters some evidence classifications, making the corresponding conclusions reference-conditional. These findings show that lower prediction error alone does not establish transferable degradation tracking. Transfer claims must reflect the magnitude, uncertainty, and stability of the supporting evidence, without generalizing success on one target to overall method superiority.
title_zh: Evidence-gated evaluation of cross-dataset battery state-of-health transfer with a diagnostic state-of-charge proxy

title: A physics-based reduced-order model for battery voltage and state of charge prediction
abstract: When a high-fidelity electrochemical model of a specific cell is available, a reduced-order formulation can retain its predictive accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost. This work presents a physics-based reduced-order model for battery voltage and state of charge prediction, built on the single-particle model with electrolyte dynamics (SPMe). The reduced-order model is derived from a high-fidelity Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) reference that is parameterised for a large-format NMC pouch cell (57.2 Ah). A quartic polynomial profile approximates the solid-phase diffusion, and a surrogate model represents the electrolyte concentration dynamics through two modes with distinct time scales. The electrolyte surrogate is first fitted to DFN-predicted concentration profiles to establish physically grounded parameter values. These values then serve as regularisation anchors in a joint refinement of the electrolyte and anode solid-diffusion parameters against the terminal voltage. This preserves the identified time-scale structure while improving voltage accuracy. The model is tested against the DFN reference across constant-current and pulse operation, and further compared with experimental measurements on concatenated WLTC and NEDC driving cycles. Under the isothermal conditions studied ( T = 25 ° C ), the reduced-order model achieves voltage and state of charge predictions in close agreement with the DFN reference and experimental data while executing more than three orders of magnitude faster than real time.
title_zh: A physics-based reduced-order model for battery voltage and state of charge prediction

title: Development of a Data-Driven Model or Predicting the State of Health of the Li-ion Battery in an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are a key enabler of sustainable aviation, yet their gradual degradation poses a critical safety and reliability challenge, particularly for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in high-temperature environments. This study develops a data-driven model for predicting the State of Health (SOH) of Li-ion batteries using machine learning (ML). The NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) Li-ion Battery Aging Dataset (Battery #5) was used to train and test a Random Forest (RF) regression model, with features selected to capture the effects of high-temperature operation and voltage behavior. The proposed RF model was benchmarked against a Linear Regression (LR) baseline and achieved highly accurate SOH estimation, with a coefficient of determination (R^2 score) of 0.9077 and low error values, with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.2578 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.2185. These results also provide a reliable foundation for estimating the battery's Remaining Useful Life (RUL). The proposed approach supports UAV reliability and safer flight operations in high-temperature environments.
title_zh: Development of a Data-Driven Model or Predicting the State of Health of the Li-ion Battery in an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle

title: Beyond cycle-aware segmentation: Spectral–temporal relational learning for irregular battery RUL prediction
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for lithium-ion batteries is difficult when the available measurements are irregularly sampled, organized by operating cycles, and coupled across sensor variables in ways that change during degradation. Many irregular time-series methods rely on fixed-window patching and mainly model temporal correlations, which can split charge–discharge cycles and miss frequency-domain information. This paper proposes the Cycle-Aware Spectral–Temporal Graph Neural Network (CAST-GNN), which uses each operational cycle as a dual-domain modeling unit for battery prognostics. Raw multivariate records are first partitioned into cycle-aware patches using consecutive discharge-onset events. For each sensor variable within a cycle, CAST-GNN builds a raw irregular temporal view and a resampled spectral view. The two views are encoded by a Transformable Time-aware Convolution Network and by a fast Fourier transform followed by a multilayer perceptron (FFT–MLP), respectively. The resulting variable-wise embeddings are contextualized across cycles by a Transformer. Inter-variable dependencies are then modeled through a Dynamic Time-Aware Graph and a smoothed Spectral Coherence Graph, fused by a cycle-conditioned gate, and aggregated by hierarchical attention pooling for battery-level RUL regression. Experiments on the NASA, CALCE, and UNIBO benchmarks show lower prediction errors than representative baselines, and an additional experiment on commercial cells illustrates the model behavior under heterogeneous operating conditions.
title_zh: Beyond cycle-aware segmentation: Spectral–temporal relational learning for irregular battery RUL prediction
